name: AD7794BRUZ
title: Six-channel, low-noise, low-power 24-bit sigma-delta ADC with in-amp and reference
summary: The AD7794 is a 24-bit sigma-delta converter for slow, small sensor signals: six differential inputs, a programmable in-amp (gain 1 to 128), a 1.17 V internal reference and two external reference inputs. It adds excitation currents, burnout currents, an AVDD/2 bias generator, a temperature sensor and a low-side bridge switch, converts at 4.17 Hz to 500 Hz, and talks over a 3-wire serial interface. It draws 400 µA typical from 2.7 V to 5.25 V and comes in a 24-lead TSSOP.
key_figures: 24 bits, no missing codes; up to 23 effective bits
40 nV at 4.17 Hz, 85 nV at 16.7 Hz (gain 64, internal reference, chop on)
AVDD and DVDD 2.7 V to 5.25 V

pins.name: PSW
pins.function: Low-side power switch to GND.

pins.name: GND
pins.function: Ground reference.

pins.name: AVDD
pins.function: Analog supply, 2.7 V to 5.25 V.

pins.name: DVDD
pins.function: Interface supply, 2.7 V to 5.25 V, separate from AVDD: either supply may be 3 V while the other is 5 V.

pins.name: DOUT/RDY
pins.function: Serial data out from the output shift register (any register's contents), and data-ready: falls when a conversion finishes, usable as an interrupt; goes high again before the next update if not read. With CS low, each bit is put out on a falling SCLK edge and is valid on the next rising edge.

pins.name: DIN
pins.function: Serial data in to the input shift register; the communications register's address bits pick which register receives it.

circuits.title: Flowmeter: two pressure bridges and a thermistor
circuits.description: Two bridge pressure transducers (BP01, 300 mmHg full scale, 3 mV/V) sit on AIN1 and AIN2. Both bridges and REFIN1(+) are fed from VDD, which is also AVDD; the bridges' low ends return through the PSW switch to GND and also set REFIN1(−), so the measurement is ratiometric to the bridge drive. With 5 V on the bridges, full-scale output is 15 mV. Flow follows the difference between the two pressures. A thermistor on AIN3 is fed from the IOUT1 excitation current; the same current runs on through RCM to ground, and the drop on RCM is the REFIN2 reference, so the temperature reading is a ratio of thermistor to RCM and does not depend on the exact current. Opening PSW in standby takes the bridge current away.
notes: RCM's ground and REFIN2(−) meet at the same ground point.

operation.text: A 24-bit sigma-delta converter fronted by a six-way differential multiplexer, an input buffer and a low-noise programmable instrumentation amplifier (gain 1 to 128). It carries a 1.17 V band-gap reference (4 ppm/°C typical), takes up to two external differential references, and adds two programmable excitation current sources, burnout currents, an AVDD/2 bias generator, a temperature sensor, an AVDD monitor, a low-side power switch and a 64 kHz internal clock. Output rate 4.17 Hz to 500 Hz.

With chopping on, offset and offset drift are removed continuously and settling takes two conversion periods. With chopping off the update rates do not change, settling takes one conversion period, and offset must be removed by calibration from time to time. With chopping off, AMP-CM should be set to 1; that narrows the allowed common-mode range but keeps common-mode rejection from degrading.

At gain 1 or 2 the gain is applied digitally and the buffer may be on or off. Unbuffered (BUF = 0) the inputs may go 30 mV beyond either rail, so small signals slightly below ground can be measured, but the input is a switched load: series R-C on the inputs causes gain error unless kept within the R-C table. Buffered, the input is high impedance and suits resistive sensors such as strain gauges and RTDs, with inputs from GND + 100 mV to AVDD − 100 mV. From gain 4 up the in-amp is in circuit and the buffer forced on; inputs must stay from GND + 300 mV to AVDD − 1.1 V or linearity and noise suffer. At gain 64 the rms noise is 40 nV typical: 21 effective bits, 18.5 bits peak to peak.
If the external reference equals AVDD and the in-amp is active, keep the differential input within 90 % of VREF/gain.

Both ranges are measured relative to AIN(−); bipolar does not mean an input may go negative with respect to GND. Example: AIN(−) at 2.5 V, gain 1: AIN(+) spans 2.5 V to 5 V unipolar, 0 V to 5 V bipolar. The choice is the U/B bit of the configuration register.

The filter changes with update rate: sinc3 plus averaging from 4.17 Hz to 12.5 Hz; a modified sinc3 from 16.7 Hz to 39.2 Hz, giving notches at both 50 Hz and 60 Hz at 16.7 Hz; sinc4 from 50 Hz to 250 Hz; integrate-only at 500 Hz. Simultaneous 50 Hz/60 Hz rejection is best at 16.7 Hz or slower. Supply noise is rejected except at whole multiples of the modulator sampling rate.

Four lines: CS, DIN, SCLK, DOUT/RDY. Each access begins with a write to the communications register, which names the next register and whether it is read or written. DOUT/RDY falls when a new word is ready, rises after the data register is read, and rises before each update so a read is not made during it. With CS tied low the part runs on three wires and the end of conversion is found from the RDY status bit; SCLK should idle high between transfers for microcontrollers. CS can also be used as a frame sync for DSPs, the MSB then clocked out by CS, with SCLK free to run between transfers. A word may be read repeatedly before the next update (once only in continuous read). The sequence 0x08, 0x200A, 0x58 starts a single conversion and reads it; 0x58 reads a result in continuous conversion; 0x5C enters continuous read.

32 consecutive 1s on DIN reset the logic, filter, modulator and all registers to their defaults, and return the interface to waiting for a communications-register write. Reset also happens at power-up. Wait 500 µs after a reset before accessing any register. Useful when noise on SCLK has thrown the interface out of step.

Two 100 nA currents, one sourced from AVDD into AIN(+) and one sunk from AIN(−) to GND, switched together onto the selected pair by BO, with the buffer on. A full-scale reading with them on can mean an open sensor, an overloaded sensor or a missing reference (data clamped to all 1s with NOXREF set); a 0 V reading can mean a shorted sensor. Turn them off (BO = 0) for normal measurement.
Two matched sources from AVDD, each 10 µA, 210 µA or 1 mA, steered to IOUT1 or IOUT2 by the IO register, for driving bridges or RTDs.

Puts AVDD/2 on the negative input of AIN1, AIN2 or AIN3, for example to lift a thermocouple off ground so the in-amp has headroom when gain exceeds 2. It adds 40 µA of supply current, or 250 µA with BOOST set; BOOST shortens power-up into large capacitance considerably.

The internal 1.17 V reference connects straight to the modulator and is not brought out to the REFIN pins. External references are fully differential with common mode from GND to AVDD, 2.5 V nominal and usable from 0.1 V to AVDD. The REFIN inputs are unbuffered and present a dynamic load, so source R-C causes gain error. A low-impedance reference such as the ADR381 or ADR391 may carry decoupling capacitors on REFIN(+); a reference made across an external resistor should have no REFIN decoupling. When the sensor's excitation also makes the reference, excitation noise cancels; otherwise a low-noise reference is needed.

With REF_DET = 1 and an external reference selected, a reference below 0.3 V or an open REFIN pin sets NOXREF. During conversions the result then reads all 1s, so the flag only needs checking when all 1s are read. During a calibration the calibration registers are not updated and ERR is set, so ERR is worth checking after each calibration.

Four modes set through MD2 to MD0: internal zero-scale, internal full-scale, system zero-scale, system full-scale. Each result is corrected by subtracting the offset coefficient and multiplying by the full-scale coefficient before it reaches the data register. Do zero-scale before full-scale. With chopping on, internal offset calibration is unnecessary; with chopping off it is required and comes before full-scale. Internal full-scale works at any rate for gains 1, 2 and 4; at higher gains only at 16.7 Hz, 33.3 Hz or 50 Hz and below, and never at gain 128. Full-scale error does not depend on rate, so one calibration holds for all rates while gain and reference stay the same. System full-scale takes two cycles (chop on) or one (chop off) at any gain and rate. The offset registers: AIN1 to AIN3 each have one, AIN4 to AIN6 share one; full-scale registers likewise. Full-scale registers leave the factory holding gain-1 coefficients, different for internal and external reference.

PSW connects to GND through a switch of 7 Ω max (AVDD = 5 V), up to 30 mA. Placed in series with the low side of a bridge it lets the bridge be switched off in standby; after closing it again, let the sensor circuit settle before reading.

Keep analog and digital areas apart; minimum-etch ground planes shield best. Tie GND to the analog ground plane, with AGND and DGND joined close to the part, and let the plane run under the part. Keep return currents beside their outgoing paths and keep digital currents out of analog ground. Use wide supply traces. Shield clocks with digital ground, keep them away from analog inputs, avoid crossing digital and analog lines, and run traces on opposite sides at right angles. Decouple AVDD with 10 µF tantalum in parallel with 0.1 µF to GND, and DVDD with 10 µF tantalum in parallel with 0.1 µF to digital ground, placed hard against the part. Decouple other logic chips with 0.1 µF ceramic to DGND.
One grade, B, for −40 °C to +105 °C, in the 24-lead TSSOP; the Z suffix marks the Pb-free parts.
